newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. paves way for further Bel-20 slump.
newsitem.headline: U.S. paves way for further Bel-20 slump.

text.p: Renewed weakness in the United States paved the way for a further correction of the Bel-20 index in the near future, dealers said on Friday.

The Bel-20 index ended down 0.91 percent or 15.72 points at 1,714.31 in a 1,711.84/1,724.23 range after Wall Street followed up its 65-point drop Thursday with further losses Friday when stronger-than-expected economic data raised the fear of higher interest rates and sent the long U.S. bond reeling.
"If the Dow doesn't recover, we'll breach the 1,680 level Monday or Tuesday," one dealer said. He added that a test of the next support, at 1,631, was not excluded later on.
One dealer said the prospect of the U.S. presidential elections in early November would continue to weigh on markets.

Some believed that even a flurry of strong first-half company earnings would not be able to lift the morale of Belgian players and the index -- which was exemplified by insurer Fortis AG which lost 2.1 percent to 4,250 despite a firm first-half performance.
Fortis AG had already shed 1.6 percent on Thursday, despite announcing a net profit rise to 6.64 billion francs from 5.39 billion in the year-earlier period.
"It's nice but people still wanted more," one trader said.
Fellow insurer Royale Belge fared even worse, plunging 3.9 percent to 5,660 to become the day's leading loser.
"Confidence in the sector seems to have suddenly vanished," one trader said.
Banks by contrast did well, with Kredietbank and Generale Bank the only two Bel-20 gainers with a 0.5 and 0.4 percent rise to 9,670 and 11,250 francs respectively.
Holding firm Gevaert was another unexpected loser, falling 2.9 percent to 1,980. However, it announced after the close that first-half consolidated profit more than doubled to 3.77 billion francs.
